name: Hermansky-Pudlak Syndrome due to AP3B1 Deficiency

criteria.description: Presence of oculocutaneous albinism with hypopigmentation of skin, hair, and eyes
Bleeding diathesis due to platelet storage pool deficiency
Identification of biallelic pathogenic variants in the AP3B1 gene
Recurrent infections or documented immunodeficiency due to neutropenia
Electron microscopy showing absent dense granules in platelets

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of oculocutaneous albinism, bleeding diathesis, and confirmed biallelic AP3B1 pathogenic variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is confirmed by genetic testing and platelet electron microscopy.

pathognomonic.notes: Includes pale skin, light hair, and iris transillumination
searchTerms: very light skin and hair color
lack of pigment in skin and eyes
pale skin and hair from pigment loss

pathognomonic.symptomName: Platelet dense granule deficiency leading to bleeding diathesis
pathognomonic.notes: Prolonged bleeding time despite normal platelet count
searchTerms: bleeding tendency from platelet granule lack
easy bruising due to platelet storage defect

pathognomonic.notes: Predisposes to frequent respiratory and skin infections
searchTerms: frequent bacterial illnesses due to neutropenia

common.notes: Involuntary eye movements often present from infancy
searchTerms: eye shaking from lack of eye pigment
nystagmus linked to eye color loss

common.symptomName: Photophobia related to iris and retinal hypopigmentation
common.notes: Light sensitivity common in affected individuals
searchTerms: light sensitivity from iris and retina pigment loss
photophobia due to eye color defects
bright light discomfort from eye hypopigmentation
tendency to bleed and bruise easily

common.notes: Reported in some patients, possibly secondary to hypoxia or infections

occasional.notes: Usually develops in adolescence or adulthood
May be present due to immune dysregulation

searchTerms: lung artery high pressure from scarring
high lung blood pressure due to lung disease
severe immune deficiency with rare infections

laboratory: Prolonged bleeding time with normal platelet count
Absent platelet dense granules on electron microscopy
imaging: High-resolution CT showing interstitial lung disease and fibrosis
other: Platelet function studies demonstrating storage pool deficiency
Ophthalmologic exam showing iris transillumination and foveal hypoplasia

distinguishingFeatures: Pulmonary fibrosis more common and severe

redFlags: Severe bleeding episodes disproportionate to platelet count
Recurrent severe bacterial infections in infancy or childhood
Progressive pulmonary fibrosis with respiratory compromise
